html:
The Fall of Singapore was the capture of the British island fortress of Singapore by the Japanese army, from 8 to 15 February 1942. About 80,000 British, Indian and Australian troops surrendered, the largest surrender in British history.

Singapore was the main naval base of the British Empire in Asia. Japan wanted the oil, rubber and tin of Southeast Asia. On 8 December 1941, hours after Pearl Harbor, General Yamashita Tomoyuki landed in the north of Malaya. His troops moved about 1,000 km down the peninsula in eight weeks, using bicycles and light tanks. Japanese aircraft sank the two big British warships sent to stop them. On 8 February about 36,000 Japanese crossed the narrow strait to the island and took its reservoirs. Yamashita was nearly out of shells, but General Arthur Percival, with the city's water failing, gave up.

Churchill called it the worst disaster in British history. The Japanese killed many thousands of Singapore's Chinese. Some Indian prisoners joined the army of Subhas Chandra Bose. The defeat broke the belief that European rule in Asia could not be beaten, and after the war the colonies did not stay colonies for long.
